subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Mercedes-Benz engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the M166 across all six model applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The M166's application is limited to the W414 Vaneo — a compact MPV from the early 2000s. We see these vehicles less frequently now, but we retain the capability to rebuild the engine when required.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Timing chain, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every M166 rebuild.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: No widely-reported catastrophic issue pattern has been confirmed for the M166. We don't treat this engine as having one universal failure mode; diagnosis is required to establish whether an engine needs repair, rebuild or replacement.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page — they'll be added once a documented set of completed M166 rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.

typical.title: MERCEDES-BENZ M166 REBUILD
typical.intro: The following describes a typical rebuild scope for this engine — illustrative of the work involved, not a specific customer job. Real case studies from our own completed work will replace this section once available.
typical.body: The M166 is a highly-strung, high-performance engine, and its twin-scroll turbocharger is a central component in its design. A full rebuild involves removing and inspecting the turbocharger, replacing timing chain components, bearings, gaskets, and calibrating the two-stage fuel injection system (direct and port injection). Given its 421 hp output in S guise, the engine's components are stressed to a high degree, and we pay particular attention to the crankshaft and cylinder head during inspection.

scope.label: Typical Scope:
scope.text: Timing chain, bearings, gaskets, twin-scroll turbocharger inspection/refurbishment, calibration of fuel injection system
